name: Blue Finch
rangeDescription: Cerrado of interior of northeastern and central brazil; adjacent paraguay (?)
description: Slim finch with a long bill. Males are unmistakable, with indigo-blue plumage and yellow bill.

name: Cape Rock-Thrush
rangeDescription: Southeastern botswana to southern mozambique, eswatini, and cape province
description: A large, chunky, long-tailed rock-thrush. The male has a brown back and uniform blue-gray coloration restricted to the head and throat.

name: Western Wattlebird
rangeDescription: Southwestern western australia
description: Medium-large honeyeater found in southwestern Australia, typically in scrub and dry coastal woodlands. Grayish brown overall with fine white streaking; pale tips to tail feathers and chestnut in primary feathers most easily observed in flight.

name: Mekong Wagtail
rangeDescription: Lower mekong delta of cambodia and laos
description: Large black-and-white wagtail with an intricately and uniquely striped head pattern. Wings and outer tail feathers flash brightly in flight.

name: Javan Pied Starling
rangeDescription: Eastern sumatra (where possibly introduced), java, and bali; probably extinct in the wild
description: An exceedingly rare Javan endemic starling now probably extinct in the wild. Brownish mantle, black chest and upperparts, with white belly, rump, cheek and shoulder stripe.

name: Lined Forest-Falcon
rangeDescription: The guianas and southern venezuela to bolivia and amazonian brazil
description: Fierce-looking raptor of lowland rainforest interior east of the Andes; also ranges up into the foothills in a few areas. Gray with dense barring from throat to breast and an orange face (yellow in younger birds).

name: White-headed Bulbul
rangeDescription: Montane forest of southern myanmar to northwestern thailand
description: Unmistakable gray bulbul with a striking white head, rose-red bill, and orange vent. Passingly similar to white-headed forms of unrelated Black Bulbul but lacks shaggy crest, dark vent, and inky-black body of that species.

name: Green-breasted Bushshrike
rangeDescription: Montane forest of western cameroon and adjacent southeastern nigeria
description: A large, robust bushshrike with a massive head, a chunky hook-tipped black bill, and a pale eye; plumage is dull uniform olive, paler underneath, and head is gray. An uncommon resident endemic to the Cameroon-Nigeria highlands, found singly and in pairs in the canopy and at middle levels of primary hill and montane forest between 930 and 2300 meters of elevation, preferring steep slopes.

name: Laysan Finch
rangeDescription: Laysan island (northwestern hawaiian islands)
description: A finch-billed Hawaiian honeycreeper endemic to the island of Laysan; does not occur in the main Hawaiian Islands. An introduced population occurs on Pearl and Hermes Atoll.

name: Purus Jacamar
rangeDescription: Tropical eastern peru, northern bolivia, and western amazonian brazil
description: Distinctive dark jacamar with a heavy bill and short tail. Deep chocolate brown, with a pinkish bill and reddish skin around the eye.

name: Bridled Sparrow
rangeDescription: Arid central plateau of mexico (puebla to oaxaca)
description: Very handsome but rather local sparrow endemic to interior southern Mexico. Found in scrubby oak woodland and brushy cactus scrub of dry tropical foothills and interior valleys.

name: Hartlaub's Turaco
rangeDescription: Highlands of kenya, adjacent uganda, and northeastern tanzania
description: A beautiful green turaco with dark blue wings, tail, and crown. Note the white markings on the head: a white spot in front of the eye and a white line below the eye.

name: Beijing Babbler
rangeDescription: Central and northeastern china and northern korean peninsula
description: Long-tailed brown bird with a white throat, streaked back, and rusty belly. Inhabits dry vegetation, ranging from scrub to tall grasses to reedbeds.

name: Red-billed Starling
rangeDescription: Lowlands of south-central china; winters to southeastern asia and philippines
description: Large and social starling of fields, parks, and farmland. Adult’s contrastingly and sharply demarcated white head in both sexes is unique amongst the region's starlings.

name: Tennessee Warbler
rangeDescription: Southeastern alaska and southern yukon to northern usa; winters southern mexico to northwestern south america
description: Tiny, greenish warbler that breeds in boreal forest. Breeding males have lime-green back, pale blue-gray head, and dingy whitish underparts.

name: Ridgway's Hawk
rangeDescription: Lowlands of hispaniola and satellite islands
description: A scarce small hawk of forests and open woodlands. The adult is very distinctive with its gray hood and barred orange belly.

name: Mariana Crow
rangeDescription: Rota (southern northern mariana islands) and guam (where extinct; southern mariana islands, western micronesia)
description: Known to the Chamorro as the Åga, Mariana Crow is a small, entirely black crow with a dark blue gloss on the head and wings when seen well. Bases of body feathers are white, giving a ragged appearance.

name: Hoffmanns's Woodcreeper
rangeDescription: Southern amazonian brazil south of the amazon river to rondônia and southern mato grosso
description: Large woodcreeper with a strong black bill. Dark chestnut-brown overall.

name: Indian Cormorant
rangeDescription: Lowlands of india and southeastern asia
description: A dark ducklike waterbird with blue-green eyes, a rounded head, a sloping forehead, and a long and slender bill that is sharply hooked at the tip. Adults are black, immatures are brownish with white underparts.

name: Iberian Gray Shrike
rangeDescription: Iberian peninsula and southern france
description: Thrush-sized bird; pale gray overall with black mask. Found in open, dry desert and semidesert areas across Portugal and Spain, into France.
